title: Deep Robotics Tests DR02 Humanoids in Hangzhou Traffic and Tourist Areas
key_facts: Deep Robotics put a group of its DR02 humanoid robots on the streets of Xihu District, Hangzhou, China, to test them in real traffic.
Trials took place in early October in heavy visitor and vehicle traffic and steady rain, at Xixi National Wetland Park and at intersections on Zheda Road and West Wenyi Road.
At intersections the robots directed traffic, helped keep order and assisted visitors.
The DR02 has IP66 protection against rain and dust; the company used the wet weather to test outdoor endurance.
It uses onboard sensing and motion controls to move around intersections on its own, avoid people and vehicles and adjust its position and hand signals, according to Deep Robotics.
In tourist areas it was tested as a multilingual guide answering questions on routes, transport and attractions.
Peak-hour tests focused on spotting traffic violations and unsafe behaviour and giving voice safety reminders.

Deep Robotics says the aim is to take repetitive guidance work so staff can focus on judgment tasks such as managing traffic, emergencies and enforcement; it is exploring further uses in traffic management and public services.
quote_evidence: Deep Robotics has deployed a group of its DR02 humanoid robots in China’s Hangzhou’s Xihu District to test whether the machines can assist with real traffic conditions rather than controlled environments.
At intersections, the robots directed traffic, helped maintain order and assisted visitors.

The robot uses onboard sensing and motion controls to move around intersections on its own, avoid people and vehicles, and adjust its position and hand signals as traffic conditions change, according to Deep Robotics.
why_it_matters_hint: Humanoid robots are being tried in public, unscripted street work, though all claims here come from the maker.
event_date: Early Oct 2026 (exact days not given); reported 9 Oct 2026
notes: All claims come from Deep Robotics; no city authority, traffic police or independent observer is quoted, and no results or error rates are given. The article says the data will be used to refine the robot.
